documents.title: Doc 79 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 26 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 26 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage

details.fact: Car 26 (Escotto) left the track at Turn 5 on Lap 1, rejoined and gained a lasting advantage.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. The video shows Car 26 (ESC) was behind Car 24 (MCL) at the apex for Turn 5 on Lap 1. ESC drove off the track, continued through the runoff area and rejoined after Turn 6 in front of MCL. Article 27.3 of the Formula 3 Sporting Regulations provides that once a car has gone off track it may re-join provided it does so “without gaining any lasting advantage”. Because ESC was defending, he would be expected to concede the position. Because he did not do so he retained a position to which he was not entitled. Failing to lose a position that should have fairly been lost constitutes gaining an advantage. The Stewards consider this to be an infringement and impose the baseline penalty which is consistent with penalties for breaches of a similar nature.

documents.title: Doc 72 - Decision - Car 10 - Alleged starting procedure infringement
documents.subject: Decision - Car 10 - Alleged starting procedure infringement

details.fact: Race Control received a message that Car 10 did not engage the required start set- up procedure at the start of the Formation Lap for Sprint Race.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 37.5 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the Technical Delegate. During the race, Race Control notified the Stewards that Car 10 had not activated the required start set-up procedure for the formation lap. Afterwards, the Technical Deligate confirmed that, due to a late system restart in the car, Race Control received an erroneous message regarding the state of the ECU. The Technical Delegate further confirmed that the car was ECU map compliant and that the start setup procedure was in fact satisfied at the start of the formation lap. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined no breach occurred. Accordingly, no penalty is imposed.

documents.title: Doc 70 - DECISION - Car 10 - Allegedly left the track and gained an advantage on Car 1
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 10 - Allegedly left the track and gained an advantage on Car 1

details.fact: Cars 1 (Nael) and 10 (Kato) were in close quarters at Turn 18 and Car 10 went off track and reentered in front of Car 1.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (documents 67 & 68). The Stewards were requested to investigate the overall interaction of Car 1 (NAE) and Car 10 (KAT) at Turn 18. The investigation commenced from a neutral point of view meaning that neither party was alleged to be the primary offender. Instead, the Stewards examined related but separate questions: whether NAE forced KAT off track in between Turns 18 and 19 or whether KAT left the track at the exit of Turn 18 and gained a lasting advantage by doing so. Article 27.3 of the Formula 3 Sporting Regulations provides that once a car has gone off track it may re-join provided it does so “without gaining any lasting advantage”. Gaining a position constitutes gaining an advantage as does failing to lose a position that should have fairly been lost. In order to judge whether a position was gained or lost we must first determine the relative positions before and after. In this case the cars were in such close quarters at the apex of Turn 18 that it cannot be determined who was ahead at the point the cars should be judged. The Stewards, therefore, cannot make a clear determination whether KAT gained a position or merely retained one. If KAT was forced off while ahead, he is entitled to retain the position. To the contrary, if NAE had won the corner, he is not liable for forcing KAT off, and KAT would be obligated to lose the position. Since Document 69 was inconclusive as to whether or not NAE forced KAT off, it is impossible to determine here whether or not the circumstances required KAT to be behind NAE after re-joining to avoid retaining an unfair advantage. Based on the totality of these very narrow circumstances, the Stewards are not comfortably satisfied that KAT committed an infraction, and we therefore elect to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 69 - Decision - Car 1 - Allegedly forcing Car 10 off track
documents.subject: Decision - Car 1 - Allegedly forcing Car 10 off track

details.fact: Cars 1 (Nael) and 10 (Kato) were in close quarters at Turn 18 and Car 10 went off track and reentered in front of Car 1.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, 2b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (documents 67 & 68). The stewards were requested to investigate the overall interaction of Car 1 (NAE) and Car 10 (KAT) at Turn 18. The investigation commenced from a neutral point of view meaning that neither party was alleged to be the primary offender. Instead, the Stewards examined separate but related questions: whether NAE forced KAT off track in between Turns 18 and 19 or whether KAT left the track at the exit of Turn 18 and gained a lasting advantage by doing so. Clearly NAE had his front axle at KAT’s mirror at the apex of T18. However, a driver attempting an inside overtake is expected to have his front axle to the mirror prior to and at the apex. Additional considerations are how the cars arrived to the apex (was the manoeuvre made too late or was it overly optimistic?). In this borderline case, the Stewards are not comfortably satisfied that NAE established his position early enough to have won the corner. Neither are we comfortably satisfied that he failed to do so. If he had won the corner he would not be guilty of forcing KAT off. Being unable to determine whether or not NAE had won the rights to the corner it cannot be fairly determined whether or not he is liable for forcing KAT off. Since the Stewards have not reached the threshold of being comfortably satisfied with their conclusion, we refrain from taking any further action.

documents.title: Doc 52 - DECISION - Car 4 - Allegedly sole cause of Red Flag in Qualifying
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 4 - Allegedly sole cause of Red Flag in Qualifying

details.fact: The Red Flag was displayed, and the Session stopped and not resumed, following a collision between Car 4 (Stromsted) and Car 27 (David) at Turn 13.
details.infringement: Alleged Breach of Article 33.5 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 27). The Stewards conducted a hearing in relation to the incident at Turn 13 (Document 51) and determined in that hearing that the driver of Car 4 (STR) was predominately but not wholly to blame for the incident. Article 33.5 of the Sporting Regulations applies to incidents where a driver is the sole cause of the issuance of a Red Flag. Since STR was not wholly at fault for the collision it cannot be said that he alone was the sole cause of the Red Flag. Accordingly, the Stewards elect to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 51 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - Causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - Causing a collision

details.fact: Car 4 (Stromsted) collided with the rear of Car 27 (David) at Turn 13.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the 2026 International Sporting Code
details.decision: A 5-grid position penalty for both races at this Competition. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 4 points.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (documents 25 and 26). Car 4 (STR) collided with the rear of Car 27 (DAV) at Turn 13. DAV explained that he was experiencing congestion because the cars in front of him had been traveling slowly, then accelerating and aggressively braking for many corners. He stated that he was following Car 31 (XIE) out of Turn 13 while on the racing line, but that XIE did not accelerate as he expected. He then felt contact from behind and was taken out of the race. STR confirmed that the cars in front of him had been driving erratically since Turn 5. He attributed the collision to the erratic driving of the field, and not to any fault of his own. The Stewards note that a trailing car is generally held to be responsible for colliding with a car in front. The Stewards accept that the field was displaying multiple instances of erratic driving during the lap in question but determine that STR had every reason to expect it to continue. Under the circumstances, the Stewards conclude that it was not reasonable for STR to assume that cars would begin driving normally out of Turn 13 and that he had every reason to take extra caution in this situation. While the driving throughout the entire pack factored into the collision, the Stewards find STR to be predominantly at fault for running into the rear of DAV. The penalty imposed is in accordance with the penalty guidelines.

documents.title: Doc 46 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 31 - Driving unnecessarily slowly
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 31 - Driving unnecessarily slowly

details.fact: Car 31 (Xie) was driving unnecessarily slowly on the racing line while on a prep lap.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.4 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations and Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code - failure to follow Competition Notes, Item 18.
details.decision: A drop of three grid positions for both races at this Competition. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 2 points.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence and GPS data. Competition Notes, Item 18 Practice and Qualifying Etiquette provides that “drivers not on a fast lap must make all efforts to keep off the racing line” and “any driver moving slowly on the racing line may be considered potentially dangerous to any car…in line behind them”. Car 31 (XIE) was driving slowly on the racing line between Turns 13 and 14 during a prep lap. The Stewards determine that his actions also factored into many related breaches by multiple other drivers and that the ensuing situation contributed to a collision that prematurely ended the qualifying session. documents.title: Doc 36 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 15 - Leaving track without justifiable reason in Practice
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 15 - Leaving track without justifiable reason in Practice

details.fact: Car 15 (Deligny) left the track at Turn 18.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations – a driver may not deliberately leave the track without a justifiable reason.
details.decision: Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 15. This is his first Driving Reprimand of the 2026 Season.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 20). Car 15 (EDE) overtook the car in front of it by leaving the track. The driver of Car 15 (EDE) confirmed to the Stewards that as he approached Turn 18 he observed cars on the racing line travelling slowly. EDE explained that he undertook this manoeuvre with the intention to commence a push lap before the session ended. The Stewards consider the act of driving off the track to conduct an overtaking manoeuvre in these circumstances is a precarious decision because it adds risk to an already crowded situation, especially when the inevitable rejoin occurs. The Stewards find the leaving of the track in these circumstances is not a justifiable reason and amounts to a breach of the Rules. The Stewards impose a Reprimand on the driver of Car 15 (EDE).

documents.title: Doc 34 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 18 - Unsafe release in Practice
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 18 - Unsafe release in Practice

details.fact: Car 18 (Badoer) was released into the path of Car 14 (Yamakoshi) during the practice session.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 28.12 a) of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations - unsafe release
details.decision: A fine of 500 Euros to be paid by the Team. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (documents 14 & 15). The video shows Car 14 being released from its pit position by the Team and entering the fast lane. Car 18 was released from its pit position by the Team shortly after Car 14 was released. The video also shows that Car 14 had to take action to avoid a collision with Car 18. The Team of Car 18 acknowledged that this was an unsafe release the by the Team. The Stewards decide to impose a fine of 500 Euros on the Team, which is consistent with other penalties imposed for where the Team is at fault for an unsafe release.

documents.title: Doc 33 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 17 - Practice start infringement in Practice
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 17 - Practice start infringement in Practice

details.fact: Car 17 (Clerot) did not follow the Race Director instructions - practice start performed with one car directly in front of him on the grid.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code and alleged breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code - failure to follow Competition Notes, Item 15.2.b).
details.decision: Warning.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 18). The Driver of Car 17 (CLE) performed his practice start with a car directly in front of him on the grid. During the hearing, CLE explained that as soon as the car in front of him launched it went into anti-stall mode as it crept away from its grid position. CLE having already decided to perform his practice start, launched and had to pass to avoid. Competition Note 15.2.b) provides that “under no circumstances may a driver perform a practice start if another car in front of him is still stationary ahead on the same side of the grid.” Since the car in front was moving, it cannot be said that CLE violated that instruction, however the ISC provision against unsafe acts remains to be considered. In this case, the Stewards determine that CLE acted unsafely by performing his practice start before allowing the car in front to safely clear its grid position. Fortunately, this manoeuvre was not unsafe with respect to other cars. While CLE’s practice start did not expressly violate the Competition Notes, the Stewards determine that a warning is in order for failing to wait a reasonable amount of time before commencing his practice start.

documents.title: Doc 32 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 15 - Practice start infringement in Practice
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 15 - Practice start infringement in Practice

details.fact: Car 15 (Deligny) did not follow the Race Director instructions - practice start performed with one car directly in front of him on the grid.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code - failure to follow Competition Notes, Item 15.2.b).
details.decision: Warning.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 17). The Driver of Car 15 (EDE) performed his practice start with a car directly in front of him on the grid. During the hearing, EDE explained that the car that was stopped in front of him slowly advanced 4 rows up the grid before stopping again to do his practice start. Once stationary, that car then waited 12 seconds before performing his start. The stewards agree that this is an unusually long period of time to wait before doing a practice start, but determine that the delay, while a mitigating circumstance, does not excuse violating the Competition Notes. The Stewards further note that EDE’s practice start did not endanger any other cars. The Stewards determine that an infraction has occurred, but due to the mitigating circumstances elect to impose a warning which is less than the normal penalty for such an infraction.

documents.title: Doc 31 - DECISION - Car 14 - Alleged practice start infringement in Practice
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 14 - Alleged practice start infringement in Practice

details.fact: Car 14 (Yamakoshi) did not follow the Race Director instructions - practice start performed with one car directly in front of him on the grid.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code - failure to follow Competition Notes, Item 15.2.b).
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 16). The Driver of Car 14 (YAM) performed his practice start with Car 27(DAV) directly in front of him. During the hearing the driver explained that the anti-stall warning lights were flashing on DAV’s car as soon as it started to move and that the car then came to a stop with the lights still flashing. Knowing that the car in front was experiencing stall issues, YAM waited until the other side of the grid cleared and then did his practice start. DAV's team manager subsequently confirmed that DAV was experiencing issues. The Stewards take these extenuating circumstances as a mitigating factor and given that the start itself was not unsafe, elect to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 30 - DECISION - Car 8 - Alleged impeding of Car 11 in Practice
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 8 - Alleged impeding of Car 11 in Practice

details.fact: Car 11 (Gladysz) braked to avoid a collision with Car 8 (Taponen) at Turn 18.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 31.6 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations - Car 8 allegedly impeded Car 11 in Turn 18 in Practice
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and team representatives (documents 12 & 13). The video showed Car 11 (GLA) approaching Turn 18. Ahead of Car 11, Car 8 (TAP) was traveling more slowly than Car 11, and it moved to its left. Car 8's movement to the left caused Car 11 to brake and move to the edge of the circuit to avoid a collision with Car 8. The driver of Car 8 (TAP) told the Stewards that he was reacting to the situation that had occurred ahead of him, where multiple cars had slowed significantly in the approach to Turn 18. The driver of Car 11 (GLA) told the Stewards that while he was travelling faster than Car 8, he was not on a push lap and stated that he was not impacted by the incident. The Stewards decide to take no further action because the allegedly impeded driver stated he was not on a push lap and therefore was not impeded by the incident.
